nodes.label: H_old: defective draft estimator (min-max binning, Difetto 2)
nodes.rationale: Kept as a local copy only to compare readings against the corrected estimator on identical activations; the two diverge only under outliers/heavy tails (exp1: one outlier in 1001 collapses min-max by 99.7% vs 0.18% for quantile-winsorized), so on clean gaussian data the readings coincide.
nodes.norm_label: h_old: defective draft estimator (min-max binning, difetto 2)

nodes.label: D1: Quantile-winsorized binning (robust histogram estimator)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as default over min-max (99.7% collapse under one outlier), fixed range (more robust but shifts a dangerous a-priori choice onto the user), and k-NN Kozachenko-Leonenko (rejected structurally: differential entropy incompatible with [0,1] normalization, diverges to -inf on duplicated ReLU zeros, O(N^2) cost). Documented cost: attainable maximum is 99.92% of log B on continuous uniform-density data; asymmetric-quantile formula for H* corrected after adversarial review; heavy-tail (Cauchy) seed-variability caveat 4-5x vs fixed range.

nodes.label: D2: Miller-Madow correction + log(min(N,B)) normalization
nodes.rationale: Miller-Madow removes first-order bin-count bias (exp2: deviation 3.68%->0.34% at N=128); denominator log(min(N,B)) because at most min(N,B) bins can be non-empty (proved in D6), fixing Difetto 1. Clamp to 1 is a declared pragmatic convenience, not a theoretical necessity: Miller-Madow can push H_MM above the bound on exactly-uniform samples; the clamp's blind zone near the ceiling is quantified (~5% at the minimum reliability N).

nodes.label: Reliability flag criterion (B-1)/(2N) <= 0.05*log(min(N,B))
nodes.rationale: Uses B-1 (not K-1) to be evaluable a priori, independent of the data. Adversarial verification established it is a NECESSARY, NOT sufficient condition: heavy tails (lognormal sigma=2) and extreme sparsity (90% zeros, dead-ReLU regime) yield reliable=True with 7-14% error at N in [90,~200]; all probed adversarial cases fall below 5% from N>=256; B=8 mis-calibrated for heavy tails. Honest flag semantics: False = certified unreliable, True = no a-priori alarm from the bin-count bias model only. Raising the default threshold left as an open user decision (rule 05: not decided autonomously).

nodes.label: D3: Negative-activation strategies (relu/abs; shift removed)
nodes.rationale: shift REMOVED: no theoretical motivation and a discovered pathology (a constant row - the maximum-entropy case - is zeroed out, making entropy undefined). Strategy per activation module: relu for ReLU-family/Sigmoid/GELU/SiLU/LeakyReLU (negative range bounded, sign codes 'nearly off'), abs for Tanh/Softsign/Hardtanh (sign=direction, ~50% negative mass would be destroyed by relu), Softmax handled directly as a distribution, unmapped modules require an explicit mandatory choice (answers differ by up to 8.6x, so a silent default would lie). GELU/SiLU caveat: relu discards 15-24% of absolute mass for inputs concentrated near zero.

nodes.label: D4: Full-pipeline bootstrap CI, normal interval (re-decided)
nodes.rationale: REOPENED AND RE-DECIDED after adversarial verification: exp4 had validated the closed-form (Basharin) on a strictly easier problem (fixed bins); in the real pipeline quantile edges are re-estimated from the sample and that variance is invisible to the formula (coverage min 62.5%, non-converging stderr ratio 0.46-1.37 -> structural deficit). Percentile bootstrap collapses at the entropy ceiling (min 4%); basic bootstrap min 31.5%; calibrated stderr inflation rejected without test (no principled constant exists). boot-normal works because sd_boot estimates the SCALE of variability (including edge variance) while the normal interval re-centers on the point estimate H_MM. API consequence: BatchEntropy carries no per-batch stderr (an under-calibrated stderr is worse than no number); CI is on-demand via confidence_interval on raw values. Validity: read coverage as '>=85% conservative', N>=200 plane (N~400 under >90% sparsity, runtime warning), CI truncated to [0, log(min(N,B))]. Per-example entropy has NO sampling stderr by construction. Degenerate samples give zero-width CI: flag and CI are complementary, not substitutes.
nodes.norm_label: d4: full-pipeline bootstrap ci, normal interval (re-decided)

nodes.label: D5: Edge-case policies (N=0/NaN/Inf ValueError, N=1 and degenerate H=0 flagged, zero row NaN, 4D skipped)
nodes.rationale: Principle: never emit unvalidated numbers and never mask bugs of the observed network. N=0 and NaN/Inf raise ValueError (entropy undefined; silent handling would hide bugs; N=0 row added by adversarial review). Degenerate/N=1 cases return H=0 with reliable=False so true concentration is distinguishable from unestimable samples (Difetto 5). All-zero per-example rows return NaN + valid mask because 0 would lie. Conv/4D deferred by user decision: core raises, hooks skip the layer with an explicit warning.
nodes.norm_label: d5: edge-case policies (n=0/nan/inf valueerror, n=1 and degenerate h=0 flagged, zero row nan, 4d skipped)

nodes.label: D6: Bound proofs (0 <= H <= log(min(N,B)); 0 <= H <= log M)
nodes.rationale: Gibbs-inequality proofs of both bounds with attainment conditions, empirically verified in exp5 (one-hot -> 0, uniform -> log M, N<=B attainment, B|N attainment). Justifies the log(min(N,B)) normalization denominator of D2 and the winsorization ceiling exception for discrete mass in D1.
nodes.norm_label: d6: bound proofs (0 <= h <= log(min(n,b)); 0 <= h <= log m)

nodes.label: Multi-agent adversarial verification of MATH_DECISIONS
nodes.rationale: First draft was attacked by independent adversarial verifier agents (2026-07-10). Incorporated outcomes: D4 reopened and re-decided (closed-form failed its own gate on the real pipeline -> exp4b full-pipeline bootstrap); D6/D1 winsorized-maximum formula corrected for asymmetric quantiles (regressed in exp1); D5 N=0 row added; D1 H* scoping and heavy-tail caveats added; D2 reliability flag re-scoped as necessary-not-sufficient.

nodes.label: Frozen validation experiments exp1-exp5 + exp4b (validation/)
nodes.rationale: Every formula was validated numerically BEFORE implementation; each decision cites the numeric evidence that determined it. The scripts are frozen pre-implementation evidence and must stay green as part of the final gate.

nodes.label: entropylens: entropy-based statistical interpretability for PyTorch activations
nodes.rationale: Measures statistical (not semantic) properties of activation distributions without touching the model: tracked forward pass is bitwise identical to untracked, nothing enters autograd. Explicit anti-claim by design: no semantic-interpretability claims - high entropy means only 'spread out over the batch'.
nodes.norm_label: entropylens: entropy-based statistical interpretability for pytorch activations

nodes.label: per_example_entropy: per-example entropy across neurons (mandatory strategy)
nodes.rationale: The strategy (relu/abs) MUST be chosen explicitly because the two answers differ by up to 8.6x on the same input - a silent default would be a lie; unmapped modules raise an explicit error instead of guessing.

nodes.label: B1/B2/B3 bitwise-invariance guarantees (torch.equal, exact)
nodes.rationale: Outputs and gradients with/without tracking are bitwise identical (tested with torch.equal, not allclose); entropy tensors never require grad; conv/4D maps are skipped with an explicit warning rather than silently computed.

nodes.label: Honest limitations (documented, tested, not hidden)
nodes.rationale: Design principle: limitations are documented and frozen as regression tests instead of hidden - reliable flag necessary-not-sufficient, zero-width CI on degenerate samples, Cauchy seed-variability, 99.92% winsorization ceiling.

nodes.rationale: Post-hoc rendering of tracked history (near-zero training overhead), matplotlib imported lazily; rankings exclude unreliable neurons and report how many were excluded; heatmaps grey out unreliable cells instead of pretending they are measurements.
